claude-s · music-video

Boil: a kettle drums itself to the boil

Make a 12 s instrumental character music video: a stovetop kettle comes to the boil and sings at 100 degrees. 120 BPM, a papery hand-drawn look, synthesised sound, and every sound should come from something you can see.

What the skill did

  • An original brief, made to prove the skill's new character toolkit (toon.js), which was built from teardowns of the character pieces on prompt-motion.com.
  • One event list drives picture and sound. The kettle's landings are the kick, its lid rattling on 2 and 4 is the snare, each steam puff is a hat, and the water temperature steps on every 8th note to land on 100 exactly on the drop.
  • Acting with toon.js: poses land on the beat with a wind-up and an overshoot (act), hops squash and stretch with their volume kept (hop, squashAt), the face changes every two beats (asleep, curious, eager, worried, straining, laughing), and blinks come on head turns. The mug reacts 0.12 s after the kettle, answers on the off-beats, and has waited with its teabag since the first frame.
  • One continuous camera moves between framings: close on the face as it wakes, over to the thermometer it reads, wide for the hops, a slow push through the held breath at 99, then blown back out on the drop. It ends on the pour and the sip, and an iris closes on the snoring kettle.
  • Watercolour material: a pigment wash is multiplied inside each fill, the outlines boil on twos, the steam is one merged shape, and the light comes from the window and the flame.
  • Three fresh critics reviewed it against six reference contact sheets. The first two scored it 5/10 and 4/10, and their findings were fixed. The third scored it 5/10 and judged it a clearly better showcase than the previous demo.
  • The second video is the previous demo, 'Small things compound': a 29 s spoken-word lyric essay with karaoke captions, a live exponential counter and diagrams cut to a synthesised bed.

Sound

  • Everything is synthesised by sfx.py: a bed (arp, then pad, then a groove on the drop) plus about 110 cues from the same event list, mastered to -14 LUFS (LRA 13.6) under a -1.5 dBTP ceiling.
  • New character sounds. Slide is the whistle: one slide per note of the lead, up in a kettle's 1-3 kHz shriek. There is also a boing on the startle, squish and stamp on the landings, chirps for the mug, and babble, which here is a snore.
  • Half a second of true silence before the drop (-40 to -60 dBFS against -12 after it), broken only by a held breath. Then a sub drop, a steam blast and the shriek.
